definition: The mass of an object multiplied by its velocity, $p = mv$, measured in kg m/s; it is a vector, so it has a direction.
A force multiplied by the time for which it acts, $F\Delta t$; the impulse of the resultant force equals the change in momentum, and impulse is measured in N s, the same as kg m/s.
The principle that the total momentum of objects that collide or push apart stays the same, provided no resultant force from outside acts on them.
